kind_descriptions.APP: A container the platform keeps running: a web server, a worker, a bot, a queue consumer.
kind_descriptions.SITE: Files built from a repository and served straight off the node. Nothing runs between deploys.

restart_hints.ALWAYS: Bring it back whenever it stops, including after the node reboots.
restart_hints.ON_FAILURE: Bring it back only when it exits non-zero. A clean exit is left alone.
restart_hints.NEVER: Leave it stopped. For a one-shot job you start yourself.

isolation_hints.RUNSC: Syscalls are filtered in userspace. The default, and what you want unless something breaks.
isolation_hints.RUNC: Only kernel namespaces separate this from the host. For workloads gVisor cannot run, such as io_uring.

service.runc_warning: This service runs without gVisor, so only the kernel separates it from the host.

concurrency_hints.ALLOW: Start it anyway. Two copies can be running at once.
concurrency_hints.FORBID: If the last run has not finished, skip this one and say so.
concurrency_hints.REPLACE: Stop what is still running, then start the new one.

status_sentences.no_node: No node has reported this service yet.
status_sentences.archived: Archived. Nothing is running and nothing was deleted.
status_sentences.waiting_node: Waiting for a node to pick it up.
status_sentences.stopped_no_report: Stopped, and no node has reported it.
status_sentences.drifting: You asked for this to run and the node reports it {state}.
status_sentences.stopped_as_asked: Stopped as asked. Its volumes and logs are where you left them.

last_run.unreported_end: Started, and the node has not reported how it ended.

overview.archived_notice: This service is archived, which is what happens to everything in a project that gets archived. Nothing is running and nothing was deleted - restore the project from its settings and this comes back stopped.
overview.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so the controls above are off. Logs and metrics are still open to you.

state.title: State
state.stop_confirm_body_site: The node stops serving this site until you start it again. The files and every release stay where they are.
state.stop_confirm_body_app: The container is stopped. Its volumes, its logs and its environment stay where they are, and starting it again brings it back.
state.restart_confirm_body: The container is stopped and started again, so whatever it is serving right now is interrupted for a few seconds.

in_flight.start: Asking the node to run {name}. It picks the change up on its next reconcile.
in_flight.stop: Asking the node to stop {name}. Its volumes and logs stay where they are.

state.watching_node: Watching for the node to report. It reconciles every fifteen seconds, so this settles on its own.

facts.port_none: None - nothing can route to it yet
facts.releases_kept_hint: {count} - a rollback is a symlink swap, not a rebuild
facts.no_repository: None. Deploy by uploading an archive, or add one on Settings.
facts.limits_description: Enforced on the node by cgroups, and counted against your plan.

shortcuts.title: Everything else
shortcuts.deployments_hint_app: Build and roll out a change
shortcuts.volumes_hint_site: A site serves files, not disks
shortcuts.logs_hint: What it is printing right now

list.label: services
list.no_services_description: A service is either an app - a container the platform keeps running - or a static site built from a repository. Add the first one and it will show up here with whatever the node reports about it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description_archived: This service is archived. Restore its project before changing anything.
settings.description_active: Saving publishes a new spec. The node applies it on its next reconcile.
settings.archived_notice: Archived services are read-only here. Restore the project from its settings screen.
settings.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so this form is off.
settings.address_hint: Address: /{slug}. It cannot be changed - something is always still pointing at the old one.
settings.container_description: What the node runs, and how it keeps it running.
settings.source_description_site: A site is built from a repository, and the build produces the directory the node serves.
settings.source_description_app: Optional for an app: how your code gets into a language-runtime image.
settings.limits_description: Enforced by the node through cgroups.

delete.title: Delete
delete.description_site: Removes the site, its releases and its domains. The published files stay on the node until they are purged.
delete.description_app: Removes the container, its environment, its volumes mounts and its scheduled commands. Volume data stays on the node until it is purged.
delete.confirm_body: The service is removed from the node and from this project. Volume data is kept on the node until an operator purges it; everything else about this cannot be undone.
delete.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so this is off.

resources.disk_hint: The container's own writable layer. Volumes are separate and are added later.
resources.pids_hint: Enough for a runtime and its workers, few enough to stop a fork bomb taking the node with it.
resources.placement_tags_hint: Optional. Only nodes carrying every tag are considered. Separate them with commas.

runtime.image_hint: Including the tag. A digest is recorded once the node has pulled it.
runtime.command_hint: Optional. Overrides the image's CMD. Quote an argument that contains spaces.
runtime.entrypoint_hint: Optional. Leave empty unless the image's own entrypoint gets in the way.
runtime.working_dir_hint: Optional. A path inside the container, so it starts with a slash.
runtime.port_hint: The port the app listens on inside the container. Needed before a domain can reach it, and before a health check has anything to probe.
runtime.health_check_hint: Optional, and it needs the port above. A 2xx means healthy.
runtime.probe_hint: Between every second and every hour.

repository.repo_hint: An https:// or ssh:// URL, or the git@host:owner/repo form.
repository.branch_hint: Which branch a deployment builds from.
repository.credential_stored_hint: One is stored. Leave this empty to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.
repository.credential_empty_hint: Only needed for a private repository. It is encrypted before it is stored.
repository.auto_deploy_hint: The webhook URL is on the deployments screen once the service exists.

build.choose_preset_placeholder: Choose how the site is built
build.no_build_option: No build - the image is the app
build.command_placeholder_preset: Leave empty for the preset default
build.command_hint_custom: A custom build needs the command that produces the site.
build.command_hint_preset: Optional. The preset already knows how to build this.
build.output_dir_hint: Relative to the repository. It cannot start with a slash or contain ".." - the node resolves it under the build's own tree.
build.keep_releases_hint: Older builds stay on the node so a rollback is a symlink swap rather than a rebuild. Between 1 and 50.

isolation.label: Isolation
isolation.reason_hint: Say which workload cannot run under runsc. This is shown next to the service.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description_site: A static site has no running process, so everything here is read while it builds.
environment.description_app: Handed to the container as its environment. A change reaches the workload the next time it starts.
environment.archived_notice: This service is archived, so its environment is read-only. Restore the project from its settings screen.
environment.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so the controls on this page are off.
environment.rules_footer: A name belongs to one list or the other: adding a secret called API_KEY is refused while a plain variable of that name exists, and the other way round. WISPER_* is reserved for values the platform sets itself.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Readable values, handed to the container as its environment.
variables.empty_description: Anything the workload reads from its environment goes here - a port, a log level, the address of something it talks to. Values that must not be readable belong in the secrets list below.
variables.dialog_edit_desc: The new value reaches the container the next time it starts.
variables.dialog_new_desc: A plain variable: its value is readable on this screen and by anyone who can open it.
variables.name_hint_edit: A name cannot be changed. Remove this one and add the new name.
variables.name_hint_new: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit. WISPER_* is reserved.
variables.value_hint: Anything but a null byte. Put anything larger than 32 KB on a volume instead.
variables.build_time_hint_site: A static site has no running process, so a variable is only ever read during the build.
variables.build_time_hint_app: On for anything the build needs - an npm token, a public API base URL.
variables.remove_confirm_body: The container stops seeing it the next time it starts.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.description: Encrypted at rest and write-only from here. The container reads them as ordinary environment variables.
secrets.empty_description: Anything you would not want on the screen behind you - a database password, an API key, a signing secret. It goes into the container's environment exactly like a plain variable; the difference is that nothing here can read it back.
secrets.count_label: {count} {count, plural, one {secret} other {secrets}}, values not readable
secrets.dialog_rotate_desc: The panel cannot show you the current value. Saving replaces it.
secrets.dialog_new_desc: Encrypted before it is stored. Nothing in the panel can show it back to you.
secrets.name_hint_new: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit. WISPER_* is reserved, and a plain variable of the same name would clash.
secrets.value_hint: Up to 32 KB. Anything larger belongs in a file on a volume, not in the environment.
secrets.build_time_hint_app: On for anything the build needs - a private registry token, a source-map upload key.
secrets.remove_confirm_body: The container stops seeing it the next time it starts, and the panel cannot give the value back afterwards.

volumes.title: Volumes
volumes.description_site: A static site is files on disk already, so there is nothing to mount into it.
volumes.description_app: Directories on the node that outlive the container. Attaching one pins this service to its node.
volumes.nothing_to_mount_body: A static site has no running container, so there is nothing for a volume to appear inside. The files this site publishes are on the node already - open the file manager to browse, edit or upload them, and the deployment history to roll a release back.
volumes.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so the controls on this page are off.
volumes.archived_notice: This service is archived. Its volumes are intact and nothing was deleted - restore the project from its settings screen to change them again.
volumes.attached_card_desc: {count} {count, plural, one {volume} other {volumes}} on this service.
volumes.empty_desc: Everything the container writes outside a volume is lost the next time it is recreated - on a redeploy, an image change, a node reboot. Anything you want to keep goes on a volume.
volumes.quota_foot_single: This volume counts for {percent}% of your disk quota. Detaching one leaves its data on the node until an operator purges it, so the space is freed against the plan but the files are still recoverable.
volumes.quota_foot_multi: These volumes count for {percent}% of your disk quota. Detaching one leaves its data on the node until an operator purges it, so the space is freed against the plan but the files are still recoverable.
volumes.not_measured_aria: {name} has not been measured by a node yet
volumes.dialog_edit_desc: Mounted at {mountPath}. The quota is what the node enforces on the directory.
volumes.dialog_new_desc: A directory on the node that survives restarts, redeploys and image changes.
volumes.detach_confirm_body: Nothing is mounted at {mountPath} afterwards. The data stays on the node until it is purged, but the service loses its way to it and is no longer pinned by it.
volumes.name_hint_edit: A name cannot be changed: it is what identifies the directory on the node.
volumes.name_hint_new: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. Left empty it becomes "data".
volumes.mount_path_hint_edit: A mount path cannot be moved. Detach this volume and attach a new one to change it.
volumes.mount_path_hint_new: An absolute Linux path inside the container. Not /, /etc, /usr or anywhere the image keeps its own files.
volumes.size_hint_range: Between 1 MiB and 4 TiB, counted against your organization’s disk quota.
volumes.size_hint_with_used: Between 1 MiB and 4 TiB, counted against your organization’s disk quota. {used} is already stored, so it cannot go below that.
volumes.read_only_hint_edit: Fixed once attached, because a workload that opened it for writing would have to be restarted anyway.
volumes.read_only_hint_new: For a volume the container only reads - configuration, a shared asset bundle.
volumes.backups_hint_edit: Set when the volume is attached. Detach and attach again to change it.
volumes.backups_hint_new: On unless this holds a cache you would rather not pay to store twice.

tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
tasks.description_site: A static site has no container, so there is nothing for a scheduled command to run inside.
tasks.description_app: Run by the node inside this container. They keep firing while the panel is unreachable.
tasks.nothing_to_run_body: A static site is files on disk; there is no process to run a command in. If the site needs something rebuilt on a schedule, the thing to schedule is a deployment - or put the command on an app service in the same project, which does have a container.
tasks.failing_single: {name} ended badly on its last run.
tasks.failing_multi: {count} of these ended badly on their last run.
tasks.failing_explanation: A schedule that fires correctly and a command that exits non-zero look the same from the outside - open the row for the exit code and whatever the node reported.
tasks.read_only_notice: You have read access to this organization, so the controls on this page are off.
tasks.archived_notice: This service is archived, so nothing here is running. Restore the project from its settings screen to schedule commands again.
tasks.commands_card_desc: {count} scheduled{off, select, 0 {} other {, {off} switched off}}. {used} of {limit} allowed on your plan.
tasks.empty_desc: A queue worker's nightly prune, a database vacuum, a report at 6am. The node keeps the schedule itself, so these keep running even when the panel is down.
tasks.footer_hint: Commands run without a shell: the line is split into arguments and executed directly, so a pipe or a redirect has to go inside a script the container already has. Output goes to the container's logs.
tasks.no_further_run: No further run could be worked out from this schedule.
tasks.switched_off_hint: Switched off. Its schedule and history are kept.
tasks.dialog_description: The node runs it inside this service's container and keeps the schedule even while the panel is unreachable.
tasks.remove_confirm_body: The command stops being scheduled, and its run history goes with it.
tasks.name_hint_edit: A name cannot be changed: it is what identifies this entry. Remove it and add the new name.
tasks.name_hint_new: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. It is how this entry is identified.
tasks.command_hint: Split into arguments the way a shell would, then run directly - there is no shell in between, so pipes and redirects do not work here.
tasks.schedule_default_hint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
tasks.timezone_hint: An IANA name such as Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Left empty it is UTC - which is what a job that must not move twice a year wants.
tasks.timeout_hint: The node kills the run at this point and records it as failed.
tasks.concurrency_label: If the last run is still going
tasks.enabled_hint: Off keeps the entry and its history but stops the node running it.
